parole.significato: A regional military governor in China during the Tang dynasty and the Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms period.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Mandarin 節度使 /节度使 (jiédùshǐ) via Hanyu Pinyin.

parole.significato: A rare mineral first discovered in Tibet in 2009.
parole.testo: From Mandarin 青松 (qīngsōng) via Hanyu Pinyin, the first name of Chinese geologist Qingsong Fang (1939–2010) who discovered the mineral, + -ite.

parole.significato: A sweet rice-flour ball, usually filled with red bean paste, traditionally consumed on Tomb Sweeping Day in China.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Mandarin 青團／青团 (qīngtuán) via Hanyu Pinyin.
Borrowed from Mandarin 拳法 (quánfǎ) via Hanyu Pinyin. Doublet of kenpo.

parole.significato: A kiln in which Chinese Ru ware was manufactured during the Song dynasty.
parole.testo: Partial calque of Mandarin 汝窯 /汝窑 (Rǔyáo), using the Hanyu Pinyin romanization of Mandarin 汝 (Rǔ), in reference to Ruzhou, where they were located.

parole.significato: A very rare type of Chinese porcelain, often with a blue glaze, dating from the Song dynasty.
parole.testo: Partial calque of Mandarin 汝瓷 (Rǔcí), using the Hanyu Pinyin romanization of Mandarin 汝 (Rǔ), in reference to the town of Ruzhou where it was manufactured.
